name: spawn
summary: One saved launch record per provider account, ordinary host-ticket execution and a pane-free host-local managed connection, with durable reservations and explicit outcomes.
way_in: After explicit installation or linking of the discovered package path, open SPAWN from the status/menu entry, command palette, or Files pane beside WORK. The main action opens a real right-hand SPAWN pane: Setup with Guided setup first until a reviewed configured agent exists, otherwise Start an agent. Current agents, single-agent starts and agent settings are ordinary controls; JSON, transport diagnostics and recovery remain Advanced.
scope: Launches stay in the captured current Tern host/session. SPAWN does not create or switch sessions, trust or reconnect hosts, create OS accounts, copy credentials, or automatically clean up sessions.

configuration.owner: Execution-host SPAWN authority; the desktop window journal is not a second roster authority.
configuration.storage: Host tern.kv key authority uses a version-4 envelope with configuration, config_revision, setup lifecycle and session-scoped launch/job/reply/request watermarks. Jobs store record ID, config revision and display fields, not a record copy. Non-empty legacy pending inputs remain blocked rather than silently discarded. Snapshot and request envelopes remain version 2; SPAWN_STATE_V2 is an Advanced machine projection. Configuration retains outer schema 2 and schema-2 host agent buckets. Managed attempts preserve their observer identity and have no ordinary execution job or ticket. The saved namespace identifies the exact roster.
configuration.validation: An actual reviewed command and string-array arguments are required. Native OMP is OMP-only; prompt is an OMP setting. All saves use optimistic config revisions. Original migration sources are preserved; differing host/client copies, including explicit empty sources, require per-record selection or omission and confirmation. Unknown or corrupt data fails visibly rather than resetting. Full-record JSON editing preserves the stable ID and validates every managed field, then requires separate explicit settings approval; JSON cannot self-approve. Managed declarations and operator attestations are configuration, not machine proof.
configuration.limits: 32 records; 128 attempts per session; 64 pending requests/results and observer watermarks; 120000-byte state/snapshot ceiling. Every saved write keeps only the 26 newest finished attempts per session (clear-history eligibility) with their jobs, and each verified Config inventory automatically forgets sessions absent from it unless they are current or still have an active launch. At transport capacity, retire the generation and refuse the triggering request without executing it; preserve jobs/history. Other capacity errors remain visible. Active and unresolved attempts are never evicted. Managed bridge references are retained across ordinary history trimming and absent-session forgetting; transport reset must also respect managed owners, unresolved execution and import gates.

setup: Guided setup uses the effective configured default agent in Tern settings, including with an empty saved roster; it does not require OMP or inspect conversations. A missing, null or blank default fails visibly: Set a default agent in Tern settings, then try setup again. A provider-neutral skill gathers the answers and an explicit helper submits the completed configuration bound to the active setup run and execution host. The user reviews the complete submitted records and confirms import into the original host/session. Advanced recovery references the immutable retained result and requires fresh confirmation; it does not reread a file or scrape a transcript. Manual Config creation and paste/review/confirm JSON remain available without a default agent. Import never launches accounts; identical records are skipped and conflicting IDs refuse the whole import rather than overwriting saved configuration.

backends.native-agent: Ordinary Native OMP uses the same harmless host-ticket allocation and host executor as ordinary terminal records, preserving its configured command/cwd and approved nonempty startup prompt. It requires a reviewed POSIX execution-host shell; unverified Windows ordinary native launch parsing is refused. Managed Native OMP is the documented exception described below.
backends.local-terminal: Terminal: the window allocates only a harmless host-issued ticket. The host prepares admitted tickets, captures one matching ticket and its native shell in memory within the spawn filter, then durably claims the pane outside that filter. Scope/readiness and persisted submission intent precede the single provider invocation; output remains after completion.
backends.ssh-command: SSH terminal: SSH invoked from the retained execution-host parent shell, optional destination user/key path, POSIX destination command quoting. Forced-command routes retain their own installed entrypoint policy.

shells: Rendering uses the execution host's actual SpawnSpec.program, never desktop SDK shell metadata. Supported: non-Windows sh/bash/dash/ksh/zsh or pwsh/powershell including .exe. Windows ProcessStartInfo preserves argv; batch escaping and a short-lived status carrier preserve child status. cmd.exe as parent and unknown shells are refused. Terminal input refuses control bytes other than LF before submission. Existing script-execution policy is respected without bypass. Managed execution instead uses the host-built fresh-launch contract and explicit host/target shell declarations; it does not claim to observe an ordinary ticket pane shell. Shared resolution preserves exact configured OS-user and SSH destination identity.
startup_prompts: Approved role prompts are saved record values edited or imported through Config, not a hard-coded policy button or global OMP default. Existing custom prompts require explicit review. Prompts are startup arguments delivered once per new launch, never resent on reload/reconnect; observed delivery is not proof of orchestration readiness.
transport: Only the host writes authority. Admission, watermark and keyed reply persist in one atomic write; admission itself executes nothing. Definitive refusals return an in-memory reply to the requesting observer at once. The window allocates a harmless ticket and the host claims it before one persisted-intent provider write. Old identities/sequences, changed request reuse and stale config are rejected. Transport capacity rotates only its generation and refuses the triggering request; explicit refresh/reopen is required, never automatic replay. Manual reset additionally requires no pending/unreviewed results and no live or managed attempts. Jobs/history and live host completion tracking survive generation rotation. A pending request whose retained host reply is a definitive refusal is acknowledged automatically; nothing was executed.
runtime: Current agents separates active SPAWN observations from failed/exited history and read-only Other Tern sessions; history and diagnostics remain Advanced. Host completion outranks wrapper idle state. The existing host sweep settles ordinary attempts against actual native pane inventory and the bounded Linux daemon-epoch grace; unverifiable host state remains unknown, not stopped. Settlement never closes/kills a managed conversation. Each explicit saved-agent row starts exactly one agent; multi-agent orchestration belongs to ORCH+. Main palette navigation uses the real right-hand pane and has no floating launch submenu. Guided setup starts the configured native default once, arranges it left of SPAWN, submits one immutable run-bound result for review, and reports success only after the supported writer commits/readbacks the approved roster. Routine same-native-conversation reconnect rebinds only when exact retained identity and quiescent effect journals prove it; unknown effects remain held.
duplicates: Every Spawn creates a new host-owned attempt; one record may run any number of copies, and only disabled records are skipped. There is no manual release: ordinary attempts settle themselves (see runtime). Retained resolve_attempt / resolve_lost_attempts requests from older versions are acknowledged as obsolete and never replayed.
codex: Account-owned executable/package tree, npm prefix/cache and updater environment; separate approved provisioning and owner-approved updates. SSH account wrappers explicitly invoke a fixed, identity-checked launcher for their account; forced keys ignore the equivalent supplied command and unforced keys execute that same launcher. Wrappers and entrypoint return true provider/SSH status without nested shell retention or shared executable fallback. Verify each client's alias/account routing. Existing sessions, credentials, unrelated shared installation and approval policies remain unchanged.
normal_plus: Ordinary + remains Tern's built-in new-tab behavior. Files SPAWN coexists beside WORK; linking/reloading starts no saved accounts.
state: Only non-secret settings, migration originals and observation/transport metadata are stored. Key paths are allowed; passwords, tokens, key contents and passphrases are not. Host authority and client journals may occupy different machines' plugin-data stores.
delivery: Discover package/link/config/data paths separately on every host and client machine. Back up code, links and affected host/client plugin data before explicitly approved deployment. Rollback restores matching code and data only with explicit consent because newer edits/outcomes can be lost. Separate Tern session cleanup is inspect/select/confirm only. No deployment, visual pass or completed platform matrix is asserted by this metadata.

managed_dispatch.surface: The host-local plugin carrier conveys bounded dispatch protocol v2 responses and private SPAWN_EXECUTION v2 projections through the actual ORCH+ panel. No parked transport tab or background product daemon is required. Advanced retains the non-palette spawn.dispatch diagnostic block; ordinary SPAWN uses its existing ticket path.
managed_dispatch.window_exception: Only managed launches and separately claimed native_wake grants use dispatch_window effects. The host builds approved fresh command bytes; the exact granted window executes new_tab or agents:start. Managed panes carry no ordinary ticket and are not intercepted by the host ticket executor. This is a deliberate managed native/window exception, not an alternate ordinary command builder.
managed_dispatch.identity: The actual ORCH+ source panel, execution host, native session, window-scoped origin, peer incarnation and immutable launch/mailbox bindings must match. A carrier message or display label is not authority. Ordinary Config retains its captured-native-window verification.
managed_dispatch.lifecycle: Catalog, launch, accept, status, roster import, mailbox operations, separately claimed native_wake, attach_worker, exact native stop and settled retirement follow managed-domain receipts. Unknown effects are never automatically retried. Reconnect handles verifiable paired steps; uncertainty stays visible without asking users to drive routine transport actions.
managed_dispatch.transport: Managed ownership is session/namespace scoped across ordinary transport-generation rotation. Saved panel state is only a view cursor. The bounded host-local carrier transports existing messages; reducers and fresh exact claims remain the authority for effects.
